import requests

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:3000"
TIMEOUT = 30

def test_health_check_api_returns_server_status_and_timestamp():
    url = f"{BASE_URL}/api/health"
    try:
        resp = requests.get(url, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert resp.status_code == 200, f"Expected status code 200, got {resp.status_code}"
        data = resp.json()
        assert isinstance(data, dict), "Response JSON is not a dictionary"
        for field in ["status", "message", "timestamp"]:
            assert field in data, f"Missing field '{field}' in response"
            assert isinstance(data[field], str), f"Field '{field}' is not a string"
        assert data["status"].lower() in ("ok", "running", "healthy", "up", "success", "alive") or len(data["status"]) > 0, "Status string unexpected or empty"

        assert len(data["message"]) > 0, "Message field is empty"
        assert len(data["timestamp"]) > 0, "Timestamp field is empty"
    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
        assert False, f"Request failed: {e}"

import requests

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:3000"
LOGIN_URL = f"{BASE_URL}/api/auth/login"
AUTH_ME_URL = f"{BASE_URL}/api/auth/me"
TIMEOUT = 30

def test_authentication_api_get_current_user_with_valid_token():
    # Step 1: Login as admin to obtain valid token
    login_payload = {
        "username": "jose",
        "password": "password123"
    }
    login_resp = requests.post(LOGIN_URL, json=login_payload, timeout=TIMEOUT)
    assert login_resp.status_code == 200, f"Login failed with status {login_resp.status_code}"
    login_data = login_resp.json()

    token = login_data["token"]
    assert "user" in login_data, "Login response missing user object"
    user = login_data["user"]

        "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"
    }
    auth_me_resp = requests.get(AUTH_ME_URL, headers=headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
    assert auth_me_resp.status_code == 200, f"/api/auth/me failed with status {auth_me_resp.status_code}"
    auth_me_data = auth_me_resp.json()
    assert "user" in auth_me_data, "Response missing user object"
    current_user = auth_me_data["user"]
    for field in ("id", "username", "fullName", "role"):
        assert field in current_user, f"Authenticated user object missing field: {field}"

title: TC007-user management list users with admin token
description: Test GET /api/users with a valid admin Authorization Bearer token to verify it returns a 200 status with { users: [...] } array, no password hashes in any user object.
code:
import requests

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:3000"
ADMIN_USERNAME = "jose"
ADMIN_PASSWORD = "password123"
TIMEOUT = 30

def test_user_management_list_users_with_admin_token():
    login_url = f"{BASE_URL}/api/auth/login"
    users_url = f"{BASE_URL}/api/users"

    # Login as admin to obtain token
    login_payload = {"username": ADMIN_USERNAME, "password": ADMIN_PASSWORD}
    try:
        login_resp = requests.post(login_url, json=login_payload, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        login_resp.raise_for_status()
    except requests.RequestException as e:
        assert False, f"Admin login request failed: {e}"
    login_data = login_resp.json()
    assert "token" in login_data and isinstance(login_data["token"], str), "Token missing in login response"

    token = login_data["token"]
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}

    # Request list of users
    try:
        resp = requests.get(users_url, headers=headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        resp.raise_for_status()
    except requests.RequestException as e:
        assert False, f"GET /api/users request failed: {e}"

    assert resp.status_code == 200, f"Expected 200 status, got {resp.status_code}"

    data = resp.json()
    assert "users" in data and isinstance(data["users"], list), "Response JSON missing 'users' array"

    # Validate no password hashes and presence of user fields
    for user in data["users"]:
        assert isinstance(user, dict), "Each user entry must be a dict"
        # Ensure password hash not present by checking no keys like 'password' or 'passwordHash'
        assert "password" not in user and "passwordHash" not in user, "User object contains password hash"

        # Verify expected fields exist: at least id, username, fullName, role, isActive (based on typical user object)
        # Since PRD shows user objects returned in {users: User[]} with no password hashes, we assert typical fields exist
        assert "id" in user and isinstance(user["id"], int), "User object missing id or id is not int"
        assert "username" in user and isinstance(user["username"], str), "User object missing username or incorrect type"
        assert "fullName" in user and isinstance(user["fullName"], str), "User object missing fullName or incorrect type"
        assert "role" in user and isinstance(user["role"], str), "User object missing role or incorrect type"
        # isActive might be included, if present check type
        if "isActive" in user:
            assert isinstance(user["isActive"], bool), "User isActive field is not boolean"

title: TC023-dashboard valuation returns inventory value by location
description: Test GET /api/dashboard/valuation with Bearer token. Expect 200 with { adel: number, calhoun: number, total: number }. All values non-negative. total must equal adel + calhoun within 0.01 tolerance.
code:
import requests

def test_dashboard_valuation_returns_inventory_value_by_location():
    base_url = "http://localhost:3000"
    login_url = f"{base_url}/api/auth/login"
    valuation_url = f"{base_url}/api/dashboard/valuation"
    username = "jose"
    password = "password123"
    timeout = 30

    # Step 1: Authenticate to obtain Bearer token
    try:
        login_resp = requests.post(
            login_url,
            json={"username": username, "password": password},
            timeout=timeout
        )
        login_resp.raise_for_status()
    except requests.RequestException as e:
        assert False, f"Login request failed: {e}"

    login_data = login_resp.json()
    assert "token" in login_data, "Login response missing token"
    token = login_data["token"]
    assert isinstance(token, str) and token != ""

    headers = {
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"
    }

    # Step 2: Request dashboard valuation
    try:
        val_resp = requests.get(valuation_url, headers=headers, timeout=timeout)
        val_resp.raise_for_status()
    except requests.RequestException as e:
        assert False, f"GET /api/dashboard/valuation failed: {e}"

    # Validate response status code 200
    assert val_resp.status_code == 200, f"Expected 200, got {val_resp.status_code}"

    data = val_resp.json()
    expected_keys = {"adel", "calhoun", "total"}
    assert isinstance(data, dict), "Response is not a JSON object"
    assert expected_keys.issubset(data.keys()), f"Response keys missing, expected at least {expected_keys}"

    adel = data["adel"]
    calhoun = data["calhoun"]
    total = data["total"]

    # All values must be numbers and non-negative
    for val in (adel, calhoun, total):
        assert isinstance(val, (int, float)), f"Value {val} is not a number"
        assert val >= 0, f"Value {val} is negative"

    # total must equal adel + calhoun within 0.01 tolerance
    diff = abs(total - (adel + calhoun))
    assert diff <= 0.01, f"total {total} does not equal adel + calhoun {adel + calhoun} within 0.01 tolerance (diff={diff})"

test_dashboard_valuation_returns_inventory_value_by_location()

title: TC024-dashboard activity feed returns recent transactions with human readable descriptions
description: Test GET /api/dashboard/activity with Bearer token. Expect 200 with { activity: [...] }. Array length <= 20. An empty array is valid. IMPORTANT: Each entry has these exact fields: id (number), description (non-empty string), transactionType (string — NOT 'type'), location (string), transactionDate (string), createdAt (string). Assert entry['transactionType'] NOT entry['type'].
code:
import requests

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:3000"
ADMIN_USERNAME = "jose"
ADMIN_PASSWORD = "password123"
TIMEOUT = 30


def test_dashboard_activity_feed_returns_recent_transactions_with_human_readable_descriptions():
    # Login as admin to get token
    login_url = f"{BASE_URL}/api/auth/login"
    login_payload = {"username": ADMIN_USERNAME, "password": ADMIN_PASSWORD}
    login_resp = requests.post(login_url, json=login_payload, timeout=TIMEOUT)
    assert login_resp.status_code == 200, f"Login failed: {login_resp.text}"
    login_data = login_resp.json()
    assert "token" in login_data, "Token not found in login response"
    token = login_data["token"]

    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}

    activity_url = f"{BASE_URL}/api/dashboard/activity"
    activity_resp = requests.get(activity_url, headers=headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
    assert activity_resp.status_code == 200, f"Dashboard activity feed request failed: {activity_resp.text}"

    data = activity_resp.json()
    assert "activity" in data, "'activity' key missing in response"
    activity = data["activity"]
    assert isinstance(activity, list), "'activity' is not a list"
    assert len(activity) <= 20, "Activity array length exceeds 20"

    for entry in activity:
        # Check presence of exact fields
        expected_fields = {"id", "description", "transactionType", "location", "transactionDate", "createdAt"}
        assert set(entry.keys()) == expected_fields, f"Entry fields mismatch. Found: {entry.keys()}"

        # Validate types and values
        assert isinstance(entry["id"], int), f"Entry 'id' is not an int: {entry['id']}"
        assert isinstance(entry["description"], str) and entry["description"].strip() != "", "Description is empty or not a string"
        assert isinstance(entry["transactionType"], str), "'transactionType' is not a string"
        assert "type" not in entry, "'type' field should NOT be present in the activity entry"
        assert isinstance(entry["location"], str), "'location' is not a string"
        assert isinstance(entry["transactionDate"], str), "'transactionDate' is not a string"
        assert isinstance(entry["createdAt"], str), "'createdAt' is not a string"


test_dashboard_activity_feed_returns_recent_transactions_with_human_readable_descriptions()
